correctness.rationale: Indifference gives \(V_n=n(1-e^{-\lambda/(n-1)})\). Its second difference factors exactly into a two-turn monomial polynomial R_n(z); the derivative has one interior maximum and yields one crossover. Tent-kernel weighting with a negative-to-positive single crossing proves adjacent thresholds strictly increase. Taylor expansion gives \(2-2/n-4/(3n^3)+O(n^{-4})\). The accompanying checker confirmed high-precision signs, exact rational examples, and symbolic expansion; no finite numerical test is substituted for the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The equilibrium participation formula and classical group-size effects are openly credited. No inspected primary work or published search result was found to imply the exact strict discrete curvature threshold ladder for per-group conditioned mixed Nash volunteer counts. An accessible earlier independent calculation of first differences of the same count was compared: first-difference sign thresholds control peaks and do not imply monotone second-difference thresholds. One strongly relevant 2009 paper was available only in abstract, a recorded residual risk. Hillenbrand and Winter (2017/2018) instead prove an ex-ante strategy effect when the number of players is unobserved; their full posted preprint and Proposition 1 were compared and do not imply the conditional re-equilibrated count claim.
residual_risks: Full text of the 2009 Archetti JTB article not obtained; abstract alone cannot establish whole-document noncoverage.
Unlocated equivalent Nash-count curvature result in older game-theory texts remains possible.
Behavioral and evolutionary interpretations would require different assumptions.

Hillenbrand–Winter establish an adjacent Jensen effect under unobserved group size; possible literature extending it to the present, distinct known-size conditional equilibrium may have escaped retrieval.

value.rationale: The sign of D_n exactly characterizes the effect on expected contributors per group when a group of size n is randomized to n-1 or n+1 with equal chances, holding mean size. A strictly ordered all-size threshold ladder partitions benefit-to-cost ratios into universal convex, universal concave, and single-inflection regions and yields a sharp correction to the limiting crossover. Exact rational cases demonstrate opposite changes. The quantity is independently motivated by group-size heterogeneity and is not claimed to predict real behavior.
